findings.title: Clone retains the original map as its eviction-hook owner
findings.body: `targetMap.copy()` constructs the cloned table with the old table's `hookOwner`, so the clone still calls `removeEldestEntry` on the original map. For a subclass overriding that hook, inserting into the clone can invoke callbacks on the original, remove the original's case-insensitive alias, and leave the clone's alias table stale when an eldest entry is evicted. It also keeps the original map reachable from the clone. Rebind the copied target table to the newly constructed map rather than copying the old owner reference.

findings.title: PlainText mode rejects the exact postimage on a normal Java-source run
findings.body: With `lst: false`, `admitted()` accepts only `PlainText`, but a normal OpenRewrite Maven/Java host parses an existing `.java` target as a `J.CompilationUnit`. Consequently the first absent-source run can generate the file, while a fresh activation against that exact installed postimage records a representation conflict and fails instead of being a fixed point. The tests mask this by explicitly reparsing every source with `PlainTextParser`. The recipe must either run the target through an actual PlainText source pipeline or safely accept the exact Java-LST postimage.

findings.title: Keep key-set containment case-sensitive like the Spring delegate
findings.body: This wrapper delegates containment to `Table.keySet()`, whose `contains` calls `Table.containsKey`; for the target table that method redirects to the outer case-insensitive map. Thus after storing `"Foo"`, `keySet().contains("foo")` returns true. Spring's wrapped `LinkedHashMap.keySet()` performs an exact-casing lookup, so this changes the public view behavior (and inherited operations such as `containsAll`). The target table's key-set containment should use its own exact-key index lookup.

originalOutput.overall_explanation: The bundle is not landable as-is: cloned maps can remain coupled to and corrupt their originals through the eviction hook, the configured receiving recipe is not idempotent under normal Java parsing, and the installed map exposes case-insensitive key-set containment where the mapped Spring surface is case-sensitive.
